predecessors.name: Mamluk Sultanate
predecessors.text: the Chouf, the Druze mountain of the Maan emirs, in the Mamluk Sultanate's Syria until the Ottoman conquest of 1516-1517

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Mount Lebanon divided on 7 December 1842 into two districts, a Christian and a Druze qaimaqamate, 'both reporting to the governor of Sidon, who resided in Beirut' (the Double Qaimaqamate)

rulers.name: Fakhr al-Din II (Maan)
rulers.title: Emir; sanjak-bey of Sidon-Beirut and Safed; Sultan of the Mountain

ledger.x: 1516: the Maan emirate of the Chouf begins under Fakhr al-Din I.
14 July 1589: Fakhr al-Din II's tax farms of Sidon and Beirut.

c. 1627: Tripoli and the coast to Latakia. He 'gained practical control of Tripoli and its eyalet, and his tax farms reached as far north as Latakia'; beylerbey of Tripoli in 1627 according to one source, which the Aleppine historian does not confirm.
1633: Kucuk Ahmed Pasha takes Fakhr al-Din.
1697: the Shihab emirs succeed the Maan.

c. 1799: fiscal authority over the Beqaa and Jabal Amil. 'After the Acre crisis, an Ottoman decree gave him fiscal authority over Mount Lebanon, Wadi al-Taym, the Beqaa Valley, and Jabal Amil'; the page gives no exact date and says he 'had little actual control over these lands'.
25 September 1840: allied forces take Beirut, Sidon and Tyre.

wars.name: Fakhr al-Din II against the Ottoman governors
wars.outcome: 1623: he beat Mustafa Pasha at Anjar in the Beqaa and became 'Sultan of the Mountain'; 1632 Kucuk Ahmed Pasha was sent to Damascus; his son Ali was killed near Khan Hasbaya; he surrendered in 1633 and was beheaded in 1635.

wars.name: Ottoman punitive expedition against Milhim Shihab
wars.outcome: An Ottoman punitive expedition against Milhim in 1748; the page gives no territorial result.

wars.name: Bashir II against Jazzar Pasha
wars.outcome: In 1789, pursued by Cezzar Ahmed Pasha of Acre, Bashir defeated his forces in the Bekaa; Jazzar 'had been acquiring Shihab territory'; relations soured again in 1799 over a troop levy during the siege of Acre; Jazzar died in 1804.

wars.name: Egyptian-Ottoman War (1831-1833)
wars.outcome: Ibrahim Pasha's forces began the conquest of Syria on 1 October 1831; Bashir offered his allegiance; Acre fell on 21 May 1832; Bashir's troops under Khalil helped take Damascus (16 June) and beat the Ottoman army at Homs (9 July); Muhammad Ali enlarged…

wars.name: Oriental Crisis of 1840
wars.outcome: 27 May 1840: Mount Lebanon's sheikhs rebel against Bashir and Ibrahim Pasha; 11 September allied naval bombardment of Beirut; 25 September Beirut, Sidon, Haifa and Tyre taken; 8 October the sultan replaces Bashir; he surrenders 11 October and goes to Malta.

certainty.note: An iltizam (tax-farm) territory with no described boundary: the Chouf core is firm, the Beqaa, Jabal Amil and the 1623-1633 conquests are the approximate part; the fiscal authority of c.
